subject: Post-call recap: control-plane isolation & air-gap feasibility (Redwood vs CloudX)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@finsecure.com>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@cloudx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: control-plane isolation & air-gap feasibility (Redwood vs CloudX)

Hi Amy (and Carlos),

Thanks again for the call this morning — solid discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of where FinSecure landed from the call
- Primary requirement: private inference with a customer-controlled control plane (no internet egress for model material) and the ability to run fully air-gapped tests for a subset of workloads.
- Secondary: integration with the existing HSM/KMS, audit logs retention for 12 months, and a predictable SLA for cold-start latency.

High-level comparison (what we discussed) — Redwood vs CloudX
- Control plane options: Redwood Private offers an optional customer-hosted control plane (VPC-hosted control plane with management plane connectors) + an on-prem packaged distribution; CloudX currently requires persistent egress to their control plane for model updates unless you choose an enterprise appliance (adds ops overhead).
- Network model: Redwood supports NAT-less peering and reverse-proxy-less setups for isolated subnets; also supports an air-gap validation mode we can run locally for duty-cycle tests.
- Evidence and compliance: Redwood can produce audit logs, per-token provenance, and an encrypted KV sync plan; we recommended a short checklist we can run with your security team.

Requested next tests (we committed to these on the call)
1) Proof-of-network: a 1-hour connectivity test to demonstrate control-plane handshake without general internet egress (we'll provide a small test harness).
2) KMS integration test: exchange an encrypted artifact via your HSM test key to validate key control semantics.
3) Air-gap dry run: a lab exercise where we load a sanitized model and run inference locally without reaching Redwood's hosted catalog (we'll provide instructions and a checklist).

Attachments included: redwood-network-options.pdf (network patterns), onprem-checklist.xlsx (security checkpoints), poc-sow-draft.docx (SOW template)

Proposed schedule
- Technical deep-dive with Monica for the KMS and network test: Wed 8/1 10am PT
- Air-gap dry run: target the week of 8/14 once we confirm test harness access

Next steps for our side
- Monica to lead technical tests and send the test harness + network playbook.
- Marissa to update the SOW and open the HubSpot deal (ROW-4391).

Amy — can you confirm the Wed 8/1 10am PT slot and whether we should include your network/security architect on the deep-dive?

Thanks,
Logan
--
Logan Wright
Principal AE, Redwood Inference

From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@finsecure.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: control-plane isolation & air-gap feasibility (Redwood vs CloudX)

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the clear recap — that aligns with our notes. A few follow-ups and clarifications from our security team before we lock the deep-dive: 

Questions from security: 
- Control plane egress: for the customer-hosted control plane, can you confirm there are zero periodic outbound calls to Redwood-managed endpoints for telemetry or model sync unless explicitly configured? We need an assurance and design doc.
- KMS/HSM: does Redwood support a bring-your-own-HSM flow with mutual TLS and certificate pinning for the key exchange? We have a Thales HSM in our lab.
- Air-gap test constraints: we'd like to define a list of prohibited telemetry during the dry run (no external calls, no model telemetry, local-only logs). Will Redwood's air-gap dry-run tooling honor that?

We can do Wed 8/1 10am PT. I'll invite our network/security architect (Rajiv Kumar) and our infra lead (Sana Iqbal). Please route the test harness + network playbook to me ahead of the meeting.

Also — please include a high-level statement in writing about how Redwood's on-prem package differs operationally from CloudX (we had a short debate on the call about persistent egress for upgrades).

Thanks,
Amy
--
Amy Chen
Director, Information Security
FinSecure Inc.
amy.chen@finsecure.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@finsecure.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: control-plane isolation & air-gap feasibility (Redwood vs CloudX)

Amy — great to meet you earlier. Short answers and proposed test artifacts below, I attached the network playbook and a trimmed checklist.

1) Control plane egress
Short answer: customer-hosted control plane can be configured for zero outbound to Redwood by running the control plane in "air-gapped mode." In that mode: no telemetry, no model catalog lookups, and no automatic binary pulls happen unless you explicitly run the packaging tool to import content. We'll provide a signed packaging artifact and instructions for manual import.

2) KMS/HSM
We support BYOHSM patterns using mutual TLS with client certs and certificate pinning. I've included an example mTLS handshake sketch in the playbook. We have validated flows with Thales and AWS CloudHSM in previous POCs — we'll provide encrypted test artifacts compatible with your Thales lab for the August test.

3) Air-gap dry run behavior
The air-gap dry-run tooling runs entirely locally. It generates local-only audit logs and a checksum manifest for all imported model files. By default we disable telemetry; telemetry can be re-enabled only via an explicit operator command (we'll show the flag).

Proposed artifacts (attached):
- redwood-network-options.pdf: contains NAT-less peering, private-link sketches, and the air-gap import flow.
- onprem-checklist.xlsx: step-by-step test checklist (control-plane boot, KMS handshake, model import, local inference smoke test).
- poc-sow-draft.docx: SOW skeleton — pricing TBD after the technical tests.

Proposed test owners & timeline
- Redwood (Monica): deliver test harness + signed artifact by Tue 7/31 EOD PT.
- FinSecure (Amy/Rajiv): run network connectivity and KMS handshake 8/1–8/3 window; share results in the 8/4 readout.

A couple of technical notes that might help in the deep-dive:
- For the control-plane handshake in air-gap mode we rely on a short-lived signed token (rotated via your HSM) rather than persistent outgoing connections.
- For upgrades: we provide a signed update package you can import manually; CloudX's appliance model typically requires an outbound check-in unless you host their full upgrade bundle yourself. Operationally that can be heavier depending on how you want to manage patching.

I'll bring detailed test steps to Wed's session.

Cheers,
Monica
